title: Leave a usable terminal after piped installation
when: Interrupting setup or resuming a suspended installer pipeline
need: The piped installer gives setup /dev/tty input. Ctrl-C quits setup; foreground resume after SIGTSTP restores its display. Mouse reporting and terminal settings must be restored before returning to the shell.
surface: Public shell installer and setup TUI
gap: No remaining terminal-proof gap under the approved combination of Terminal.app visible interruption and POSIX PTY suspend/resume tests.
review: Independent review accepted released launch.625 curl-pipe-sh interruption in Terminal.app: a readable shell returned and persistent termios matched. Only Darwin PENDIN retype-pending-input state was masked; paired transcript supplied values covered by a capture-helper window. POSIX regression additionally proves foreground ownership, the real setup driver and quit binding, SIGTSTP/fg, mouse-mode cleanup and exact stty restoration with stubbed installation side effects. The suspend test waits for the setup process to stop before fg; a delayed stop exercises scheduling where the shell prompt appears first. Source regression now delivers SIGTSTP while the main thread holds the Textual writer queue mutex: the prior handler deadlocks in Queue.put, while deferred suspension from the existing ownership timer restores the terminal and resumes. The regression also returns foreground ownership to the shell before the deferred stop; pending suspension takes priority over that expected ownership change, and the resumed app requests a full repaint. This additional lock-interruption proof is source-tested, not released live proof.
